messages.content:
The failing test `testAxisFollowing` from `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMModelTest` is trying to assert an XPath expression that involves the `following::` axis with namespaces. The test is asserting the XPath expression `//location[2]/following::node()[2]` which is expected to match `/vendor[1]/product[1]`.

The current bug report suggests an issue in the implementation of `DOMNodePointer.java`, specifically at line 120. It mentions that the code at that line only considers element and document nodes to be matched by `node()`, while it should match any node passing through there.

Looking at the `DOMNodePointer` constructor code snippet, it seems to initialize the `DOMNodePointer` object with the provided `node` and `locale`:

```java
public DOMNodePointer(Node node, Locale locale) {
    super(null, locale);
    this.node = node;
}
```

Further investigation into the `DOMModel` classes and `DOMNodePointer` methods may reveal the root cause of the issue. One potential fix could involve modifying the condition at line 120 in `DOMNodePointer.java` to always return true for `NODE_TYPE_NODE`.

Additionally, the code snippet for the `functionCount` method in `CoreFunction.java` suggests handling different types of values, including `NodeSet`. The recent bug reports related to problems with `NodeSet` and custom functions may provide insights into potential related issues in the implementation.

Next, I will suggest the locations to be fixed based on the information gathered.
```
org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.dom.DOMNodePointer.DOMNodePointer(org.w3c.dom.Node, java.util.Locale)
org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.CoreFunction.functionCount(EvalContext)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
